analysis:
The PR changes documentation only (docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md, docs/reference/configuration.md); no code changed. Security-relevant claims in the docs:
(1) Cluster runtime facts schema is bumped to v2. It adds per-model `pair_serving_grant` and `parity_qualifications`. Signed releases register `cluster_runtime`, and the coordinator derives approvals, grants and qualifications from it. This is the finding above. It touches A-005, A-017, T-052 and T-054. Coordinator-side checks live in darkbloom-platform and were not supplied.
(2) The public declaration names GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B. The docs state that some qualifications rest on an owner decision rather than cross-cable records, and that coordinator qualification applies to a whole mode family. This is disclosed, but it widens the public attack surface and trusts provider-side declarations.
(3) Qwen tensor-parallel speculative assistant is restricted to local-only clusters. `ClusterConfiguration.validate` refuses `tensorAssistant` beside `nativeMember`, and the leader refuses an approval before any part stops. This is a hardening change. I could not verify the enforcement in code.
(4) Approval fallback: quick-end counting excludes coordinator-decided ends, and a one-hour re-offer applies to the same entry. This is an availability trade-off, relevant to T-057 and T-053. A rolled-back or revoked approval is withdrawn only on the next check, which runs every minute.
(5) `darkbloom cluster local` binds the API on all interfaces without TLS by default. The docs warn about this, and I saw no change to it. The text around it was not part of the changed ranges.
A remaining question is whether the coordinator authenticates and independently approves `cluster_runtime` blocks.

findings.detail: The new text says a signed release posts `cluster_runtime` to `POST /v1/releases`, and the coordinator derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it. Qualifications for GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B are declared by the build (`ClusterPublicModels`). Their evidence is an owner decision plus a document hash, not cross-cable records, and the docs say no M5 Ultra pipeline run and no GLM TP record exists. The coordinator applies a promotable record to the whole mode family on any numerics classes, cuts and shares, so public traffic is admitted on any Apple silicon pair. Whoever can call the release API (A-005), or whoever controls a release's declaration, can now create public-serving qualification as well as binary trust. That weakens the independent-qualification assumption behind A-017, T-052 and T-054, and the threat model has no entry for this derivation path. The control is outside the supplied evidence, so the coordinator-side authorization of `cluster_runtime` is unverified. Fix: update A-005, A-017 and T-054 to cover release-derived qualifications, and confirm the coordinator requires independent approval of the `cluster_runtime` block rather than trusting the release key alone.
findings.title: Release-registered cluster_runtime now mints public-traffic approvals, grants and parity qualifications; threat model does not cover it
